candied.title: Church Supper Candied Sweet Potatoes (9x13, Never Boil)
steps: Bake potatoes whole at 400°F, 40–45 min
Cool 15 min, peel, cut 1-inch rounds
Butter 9x13 pan, lay in potatoes
Simmer butter, sugar, juice, spices 3 min
Pour syrup, add pecans, bake 375°F, 30–35 min, baste every 10 min
candied.tip: Never boil sweet potatoes—bake them whole for best syrup.

casserole.title: Sweet Potato Casserole with Pecan Crumble
ingredients: 3 lbs sweet potatoes, baked and mashed (about 4 cups)
Topping: 1 cup brown sugar, 1/3 cup flour, 1/3 cup melted butter, 1 cup chopped pecans
steps: Bake potatoes at 400°F, 45 min, cool, mash
Mix potatoes with sugar, eggs, milk, butter, vanilla, salt
Spread in buttered 2-qt dish
Mix topping, sprinkle over potatoes
Bake 350°F, 30–35 min, rest 15 min
casserole.tip: Mash by hand, not mixer, to avoid gluey texture.

cups.title: Sweet Potatoes in Orange Cups
steps: Halve oranges, scoop out, save 2 tbsp juice
Mix potatoes, butter, sugar, cinnamon, salt, juice
Fill orange shells, set in baking dish
Bake 350°F, 20 min
Top with marshmallow or pecan, bake 5 min
cups.tip: Carry them in a muffin tin so they don’t tip.

slowcook.title: Slow Cooker Candied Sweet Potatoes
slowcook.time: 4 hours on low (last 30 min lid off)
ingredients: 3 lbs sweet potatoes, peeled, cut 1.5-inch chunks
steps: Put potatoes in slow cooker
Sprinkle sugar, cinnamon, salt; toss
Dot with butter, drizzle juice
Cook low 4 hrs (or high 2.5), stir halfway
Last 30 min, lid off to thicken syrup
slowcook.tip: No water—potatoes make their own syrup.

greenbeans.title: Church Supper Green Beans
ingredients: 2 lbs fresh green beans (or 3 cans), trimmed/drained
steps: Cook bacon crisp, remove, keep fat
Cook onion in fat 6 min, add garlic 1 min
Add beans, toss to coat
Add sugar, broth, salt, pepper; cover, cook 15–20 min
Stir in vinegar, butter, bacon before serving
greenbeans.tip: Cook beans in broth, not water, for full flavor.

mashed.title: Make-Ahead Church Mashed Potatoes
ingredients: 5 lbs russet or gold potatoes, peeled, chunked
1/2 cup butter, plus 2 tbsp for top
steps: Boil potatoes in salted water 15–20 min, drain
Mash with cream cheese, sour cream, butter, milk
Season, spread in buttered 9x13, dot with butter
Cover, refrigerate up to 2 days
Bake 350°F, 30 min covered, 10–15 min uncovered
mashed.tip: Cream cheese and sour cream keep potatoes creamy.

dressing.title: Iowa Sage Bread Dressing
ingredients: 1.5 lb white bread, cubed, dried (about 14 cups)
steps: Dry bread cubes overnight or toast at 250°F, 30 min
Melt butter, cook onion/celery 10 min, add herbs
Pour over bread, toss
Mix eggs into 3 cups broth, pour over, toss
Spread in buttered 9x13, bake 350°F, 30 min covered, 20 min uncovered
dressing.tip: Use dry bread—soaks broth, keeps shape, not mushy.

corn.title: Scalloped Corn
ingredients: 1 (15 oz) can whole kernel corn, drained
steps: Mix corns, eggs, milk, onion, salt, pepper, sugar
Stir in 1 cup crackers, 2 tbsp butter
Pour in buttered 2-qt dish
Toss rest crackers with butter, scatter on top
Bake 350°F, 45–50 min, until puffed and golden
corn.tip: Half the crackers inside, half on top for crust.

biscuits.title: Sweet Potato Biscuits
ingredients: 1 cup leftover candied sweet potatoes, mashed
steps: Stir flour, baking powder, salt in bowl
Cut in cold butter until coarse crumbs
Stir in sweet potato, add milk to hold together
Pat 3/4-inch thick, cut biscuits
Bake 425°F, 12–14 min, until golden
biscuits.tip: Pat dough, don’t roll, for tender biscuits.

pie.title: Sweet Potato Pie
pie.time: 15 min at 425°F, 35–40 min at 350°F, plus 2 hr cooling
ingredients: 1.5 cups mashed baked sweet potato (about 2 medium)
steps: Mash sweet potato smooth, mix in sugars
Beat in eggs, then milk, butter, vanilla, spices
Pour in crust, bake 425°F 15 min
Lower to 350°F, bake 35–40 min, center just jiggles
Cool 2 hours before slicing
pie.tip: Push potatoes through strainer for smooth pie.

crowd.title: The Crowd Chart: How Many Pans for a Crowd
steps: For 25: 3 pans, 12 lbs potatoes (about 18)
For 50: 5 pans, 20 lbs potatoes (about 30)
For 100: 10 pans, 40 lbs potatoes
Make syrup in batches, not one big pot
Use 1/2 cup scoop to serve, 1 person serves
crowd.tip: Better to have leftovers than run out at church.
